posts.title: Choosing your first drivetrain
posts.author: Reyansh
posts.body:
Mecanum, tank or swerve? For most rookie teams, a mecanum drivetrain built from a kit chassis is the best balance of speed, agility and simplicity.

If the game rewards lining up sideways with targets, mecanum wins. If you need to push, tank drive with traction wheels is stronger.

Whatever you pick: keep the frame square, belt tension consistent and the battery low and centered.

posts.title: Odometry pods in a weekend
posts.author: Reyansh
posts.body:
Dead-wheel odometry tells your autonomous exactly where the robot is.

1. Mount two parallel pods and one perpendicular pod, spring-loaded onto the mat.
2. Convert encoder ticks to inches using wheel diameter and ticks per revolution.
3. Use a library like Road Runner or Pedro Pathing to turn readings into a pose and follow paths.

Tune by pushing the robot a measured distance and comparing.

posts.title: Wiring that never fails at competition
posts.author: Reyansh
posts.body:
Most robot failures at events are electrical.

Use strain relief on every connector, label both ends of every cable and keep motor and sensor wires apart.

Before each match: battery voltage, a tug on each connector and a quick motor test.
